3º de Primaria · Inglés · Tema 9

Can for ability

Nombre: ______________________   Fecha: ___________

Qué vas a aprender

  • Say what you can and can't do
  • Use can with all persons, always the same
  • Ask «Can you…?» and answer «Yes, I can / No, I can't»
  • Talk about the abilities of animals and robots
  • Say how well we can do something with «very well» and «a little»
  • Ask «What can you do?» and answer with full sentences
  • Use can and can't with and and but
  • Talk about abilities of people and animals in a short text

Para pensar

Un pájaro vuela, pero no sabe leer. Tú sabes leer, pero no vuelas. ¿Qué palabra mágica del inglés sirve para decir lo que cada uno sabe hacer?

Explicación

1. I can!

We use can to talk about abilities: things we are able to do. «I can run.» «I can sing.» «I can count to one hundred.» After can, we put the verb: can + run, can + swim.

En castellano: can significa «saber» o «poder»: «I can swim» = «sé nadar». Es uno de los verbos más útiles del inglés. Di en voz alta tres cosas que can hacer: «I can… I can… I can…!»

2. Action verbs

We need action verbs to talk about abilities: run (correr), jump (saltar), swim (nadar), fly (volar), climb (trepar), dance (bailar), sing (cantar), skip (saltar a la comba), ride a bike (montar en bici), play the piano, draw (dibujar) and cook (cocinar).

Play Action mime: one child mimes a verb and the class guesses: «You can swim!». Moverte te ayuda a recordar las palabras.

3. Sports and music: play

Many abilities use the verb play (jugar o tocar). Look at the two meanings:

  • play + sport (jugar a): «I can play football», «She can play tennis», «They can play basketball».
  • play + the + instrument (tocar): «I can play the guitar», «He can play the piano», «Can you play the drums?» (la batería)

Look: with instruments we use the. With sports, we don't: we never say play the football.

Other verbs for abilities:

  • ride a bike / a horse (montar en)
  • speak English / French (hablar)
  • draw (dibujar) and paint (pintar)
  • cook (cocinar)
  • skate (patinar) and ski (esquiar)
  • whistle (silbar)

Instruments to learn: the guitar, the piano, the violin, the drums, the flute, the recorder (la flauta dulce). At school in Spain, many children can play the recorder.

Activity: draw a sport and an instrument and write «I can play…» or «I can't play…».

4. Can is the same for everybody

Can is very easy: it never changes. I can, you can, he can, she can, it can, we can, they can. We never add -s: «She can dance», not «she cans dance».

And the verb after can doesn't change either: «He can swim», not «he can swims» or «he can to swim». Truco: piensa que can es como un ayudante que siempre va igual vestido, con cualquier persona.

5. I can't

To say that we are not able to do something, we use can't (cannot): «I can't fly.» «My baby brother can't walk.» «Fish can't climb trees.»

We can join two sentences with but (pero): «I can swim, but I can't dive.» «Penguins can swim, but they can't fly.» Pronunciación: escucha bien la t final: can (sí) y can't (no) suenan parecido.

6. Very well, quite well, a little

We don't do everything at the same level. We can say how well (lo bien que) we can do something:

  • «I can swim very well.» (muy bien) ★★★
  • «I can swim quite well.» (bastante bien) ★★
  • «I can swim a little.» (un poco) ★
  • «I can't swim at all.» (nada) ✗

These words go at the end of the sentence, after the activity:

  • «She can speak English very well.»
  • «He can play the piano a little.»

We can also ask: «Can you swim?» – «Yes, very well!» or «Yes, but only a little.»

It's OK to say «I can't… yet» (todavía no). Yet means that we are learning: «I can't ride a bike yet, but I'm learning.» With practice, everybody can learn new things!

Activity: write four sentences about yourself with very well, quite well, a little and not at all.

7. Can you…?

To ask about abilities, put Can first: «Can you ride a bike?», «Can your dog jump?», «Can they speak English?».

The short answers are: Yes, I can. / No, I can't.; Yes, it can. / No, it can't. En castellano: «¿Sabes montar en bici?» → «Can you ride a bike?». Solo cambias el orden: can va delante de la persona.

8. What can you do?

With Can you…? the answer is yes or no. To get more information, ask What can you do? (¿Qué sabes hacer?)

  • «What can you do?» – «I can dance and I can sing.»
  • «What can your dog do?» – «It can catch a ball.»
  • «What can a parrot do?» – «It can talk!»

We can also ask with Who (quién): «Who can speak French?» – «Marie can!»

Answer with full sentences and join two ideas:

  • With and (y): «I can swim and I can dive.»
  • With but (pero), for a contrast: «I can swim, but I can't dive.»

We can make it shorter: «I can swim and dive.» («I can» only once.)

Activity: interview a partner: «What can you do? What can't you do?» Write two sentences with and and two with but.

9. Animals can…

Animals have got amazing abilities. «Birds can fly.» «Fish can swim.» «Monkeys can climb trees.» «Kangaroos can jump very high.» «Parrots can talk.» «Cheetahs can run very fast.»

But they can't do everything: «Elephants can't jump.» «Snakes can't walk.» «Penguins can't fly.» Reto: piensa en tu animal favorito y di una cosa que can y otra que can't hacer.

10. Amazing animal abilities

Some animals have amazing (asombrosas) abilities:

  • A cheetah (guepardo) can run very fast: faster than a car in the city!
  • A kangaroo can jump very far.
  • A chameleon (camaleón) can change colour.
  • An owl (búho) can see in the dark.
  • A dolphin can swim and jump, and it can play with other dolphins.
  • A bat (murciélago) can fly, but it can't see very well. It uses sounds.
  • A snake can't walk, but it can climb trees and swim.

Remember: can doesn't change: «A cheetah can run», «Cheetahs can run».

Riddle (adivinanza): I can fly. I can sing. I can make a nest. I have got two legs and feathers. What am I? (A bird!)

Activity: choose an animal and write a riddle with three «can» sentences and one «can't» sentence. Your classmates guess!

11. Robots and superheroes

Let's imagine! A robot can do many things: «My robot can clean my room. It can carry heavy boxes. It can speak ten languages. But it can't swim: water is dangerous for robots!»

And a superhero? «Super Lola can fly and she can run faster than a car. She can see through walls. She can't cook!» Inventa tu propio robot o superhéroe y di tres cosas que can y una que can't.

12. Reading: the school talent show

Read the poster: «Talent Show on Friday! Come and see the stars of class 3A. Lucía can play the violin. Omar can do ten cartwheels (volteretas laterales). Iker and Ana can sing and dance. Mei can't sing, but she can draw a portrait in one minute! And our headteacher can juggle with three balls!»

Answer: What can Omar do? Can Mei sing? Who can play the violin?

13. Write about abilities

Now you can write a short text about what you and your family can do. Here is an example:

My name is Clara and I'm eight. I can do lots of things! I can swim very well and I can ride a bike. I can play the recorder a little. I can't play the piano yet, but I'm learning. My brother Max can play football very well, but he can't swim. My grandma can cook fantastic paella! My dog Toby can catch a ball, but he can't climb trees. What can you do?

Tips:

  • Start with your name and age.
  • Use can and can't with different verbs.
  • Say how well: very well, a little.
  • Use and and but.
  • Write about other people and a pet.
  • Finish with a question.

Activity: write your text with at least eight sentences and add a drawing.

14. Let's practise: Find someone who can…

Play Find someone who can… Your card says: whistle (silbar), touch your toes, count to 20 in English, stand on one foot, say the alphabet. Walk around and ask: «Can you whistle?» If the answer is «Yes, I can», they show you and you write their name.

At the end, tell the class: «Pablo can whistle. Sara can stand on one foot. Nobody can say the alphabet backwards!» ¡Gana quien complete la tarjeta antes!

15. Can I…? Asking for permission

Can has another important use: we use it to ask for permission (pedir permiso). We say Can I…? (¿Puedo…?):

  • «Can I go to the toilet, please?»
  • «Can I open the window, please?»
  • «Can I borrow your pencil, please?» (¿Me dejas…?)
  • «Can I have some water, please?»

The answers:

  • Yes: «Yes, of course.» (Sí, claro) / «Sure!» / «Here you are.» (Aquí tienes)
  • No: «Sorry, no.» / «Not now, sorry.» (Ahora no)

And to ask somebody to help us, we use Can you…?: «Can you help me, please?», «Can you repeat, please?» (¿Puedes repetir?), «Can you pass me the glue, please?»

Always say please (por favor) when you ask, and thank you (gracias) when somebody helps you. It's polite (educado)!

In class, these are some of the most useful sentences in English. Use them every day with your teacher.

Activity: make a poster with five «Can I…?» questions for the classroom.

16. Learning new things

Nobody can do everything at the beginning. We learn new abilities with practice. Think about babies: at first, a baby can't walk or talk. Then, step by step, the baby can sit, then stand, then walk!

Look at these sentences about the past and the future:

  • «When I was a baby, I couldn't walk.» (no podía)
  • «Now I can run and jump.»
  • «I want to learn to play the guitar.» (quiero aprender a…)

Tips for learning something new:

  • Practise every day, a little.
  • Don't be afraid of mistakes (errores): they help you learn.
  • Ask for help: «Can you help me, please?»
  • Say «I can't… yet».

And remember: we can also help other people. If your friend can't do something, you can say: «Don't worry! I can help you.»

Activity: write two things you can do now but couldn't do as a baby, and one thing you want to learn.

Can for ability

Ejercicios

  1. Traduce: correr, saltar, trepar, volar.

  2. Completa: «Birds ___ fly.»

  3. Completa: «Fish ___ walk.» (no)

  4. Pregunta: «your sister / sing».

  5. Respuesta corta (sí): «Can you dance?»

  6. Respuesta corta (no): «Can it fly?»

  7. Une con but: «I can draw.» «I can't paint.»

  8. Corrige: «He can plays tennis.»

  9. Escribe una cosa que un pingüino can y otra que can't.

  10. Escribe tres cosas que sabes hacer.

  11. How do you say «tocar el piano» in English?

  12. Complete: «I can't ride a bike ___, but I'm learning.»

  13. What can a cheetah do?

  14. In the reading, can Pip fly?

  15. What does «a little» mean?

  16. Order: well / swim / I / very / can

  17. Make a question: What / your dog / can / do?

  18. Join with and: «I can sing.» + «I can dance.»

  19. Translate: Ella sabe hablar francés un poco.

  20. What can Pip do in the water?

  21. Write an animal riddle with three can and one can't.

  22. What is the message of «Penguin can't fly»?

  23. Write a text about what you and your family can do.

  24. Write three things you couldn't do as a baby and can do now.

Practica

  1. «Sé nadar» is…

    1. A) I swim can.
    2. B) I can swim.
    3. C) I cans swim.

  2. Birds ___ fly.

    1. A) can
    2. B) cans
    3. C) can to

  3. Elephants ___ jump.

    1. A) can
    2. B) cans
    3. C) can't

  4. She can ___.

    1. A) dances
    2. B) to dance
    3. C) dance

  5. «Can you skate?» — «Yes, …»

    1. A) I can.
    2. B) I do.
    3. C) I am.

  6. «Can it swim?» — «No, …»

    1. A) it isn't.
    2. B) it can't.
    3. C) it don't.

  7. «Trepar» is…

    1. A) climb
    2. B) jump
    3. C) fly

  8. ___ you ride a bike?

    1. A) Do
    2. B) Are
    3. C) Can

  9. I can sing, ___ I can't dance.

    1. A) and
    2. B) but
    3. C) or

  10. «Cannot» is the same as…

    1. A) can
    2. B) can't
    3. C) can not to

  11. «I can play ___ guitar.»

    1. A) a
    2. B) the
    3. C) —

  12. «Bastante bien» in English is…

    1. A) very well
    2. B) a little
    3. C) quite well

  13. «___ can speak French?» – «Marie can!»

    1. A) What
    2. B) Who
    3. C) Where

  14. A chameleon can…

    1. A) change colour
    2. B) fly
    3. C) talk

  15. «I can swim, ___ I can't dive.»

    1. A) and
    2. B) because
    3. C) but

Explícalo con tus palabras

Incluye: Para qué sirve can; Por qué can no cambia con ninguna persona; Cómo se dice lo que no sé hacer y cómo uno frases con but; Cómo pregunto Can you…? y respondo.

Resumen

Glosario

Ability
Habilidad, algo que sabemos hacer.
Play the piano
Tocar el piano.
Ride a bike
Montar en bici.
Very well
Muy bien.
Quite well
Bastante bien.
A little

Yet

Who

But
Pero.
Cheetah
Guepardo.
Owl

Practise

Tarjetas de repaso

Recórtalas: pregunta delante, respuesta detrás.

canSaber / poder hacer algo.
can't (cannot)No saber / no poder.
Can you…?¿Sabes…? ¿Puedes…?
Yes, I can. / No, I can't.Respuestas cortas.
can + verboSin -s y sin to: she can swim.
butPero: I can run, but I can't fly.
climbTrepar.
ride a bikeMontar en bici.
playplay + sport (play football); play the + instrument (play the piano).
How well?very well, quite well, a little, not at all; can't… yet.
What can you do?What can you do? Who can…? and / but.
AnimalsA cheetah can run fast. An owl can see in the dark.

Soluciones

  1. B) Can + verbo.
  2. A) Can.
  3. C) No pueden.
  4. C) Verbo sin -s.
  5. A) Yes, I can.
  6. B) It can't.
  7. A) Climb.
  8. C) Can delante.
  9. B) Contraste: but.
  10. B) Can't.
  11. B) Instruments.
  12. C) How well.
  13. B) Who.
  14. A) Animals.
  15. C) Contrast.
